# Compacted Summary: Chapter 1 (Complete and Final – Updated 46)

## Setting and Time
- **Period**: Spring through late August, then Christmas/New Year period of first year; now nearly three weeks into new year (1832)
- **Primary Location**: Middlemarch and surrounding areas (Lowick, the Grange, Freshitt, Mirecombe, Salwick, Wilhaven, Quenwick, Fenmere, Bryngate, Chalky Flats, Gulton, Highbury, Cheltenham, Tipton, Yoddrell's farm, Frick, Miremere, Salmere, Riverston, Quallingham, Halsell Wood, Loamford, Brassing, Stone Court, Coldcombe, St. Peter's Place, Lowick Gate, Shrubs, Dunholt, Yorkshire, Staveton, Bilkley, Harrowgate)
- **Atmospheric Details**: Baker's boy frequently late; wind off water with salt and tar smell; dog barking periodically; bees in lavender behind parsonage; gulls quarreling over fish heads; frost silvering hedges; road rutted and puddled after thaw; children chasing hoops down lane; light going early; chalk sun on forge wall; smoke from chimneys lying flat over fields; turnip carts passing; bell for vespers ringing thinly; rain threatening since morning but holding off

## Main Characters

**Lydgate**
- **Moral Crisis**: Constructed probabilities case—Bulstrode feared scandalous disclosures from Raffles; may have tampered with patient or disobeyed orders; acknowledges "just possible" sometimes true; questions whether he would have acted identically without money; scientific conscience entangled with money obligation
- **Social Ostracism**: Patients avoiding him; practice and reputation utterly damned; general black-balling begun
- **Interview with Dorothea at Lowick Manor**: Told her everything from first application to Bulstrode under pressure of difficulties; disclosed his doubts and uneasy consciousness that accepting money made some difference in private inclination; wrote letter of gratitude
- **Final Resolution**: Declines continuing at Hospital; must get away from Middlemarch as soon as possible; will look for opening in London crowd, set up in watering-place, or go to southern town with idle English
- **Evening with Will**: Will arrived looking rather battered; felt inexpressibly mournful when discussing settling in London; Will dreaded cruelty of his outburst to Rosamond had made obligation for him
- **Return Home and Rosamond's Illness**: Found Rosamond ill on bed, soothed and tended her for next hour; imagined Dorothea's visit had raised new impressions causing Rosamond's turn towards himself
- **Morning After**: Saw Dorothea's letter on drawing-room table with check for a thousand pounds; Rosamond made no reply when he mentioned Ladislaw sat with him last night
- **Today's Visit**: Led Dorothea to drawing-room, put his letter of gratitude into her hands, then went upstairs; told Rosamond gently that Mrs. Casaubon had come to see her again; when he returned after going to Coleman's, noticed both women needed care; offered to order Dorothea's carriage

**Dorothea**
- Recently widowed; residing at Lowick Manor
- **Financial Status**: Has seven hundred a-year of her own fortune, nineteen hundred a-year from Casaubon, and between three and four thousand of ready money in the bank
- **Conviction About Lydgate**: Feels convinced Lydgate's conduct not guilty
- **Morning Resolution**: Determined to acknowledge active life before her despite buried private joy; folded herself in fatigued quiescence after sleepless night
- **Plan to Help Lydgate**: Wrote brief note enclosing check for a thousand pounds, determined to take letter when visiting Rosamond
- **Devastating Discovery at Lydgate's House**: Heard voice speaking in low tones; saw Will Ladislaw seated on sofa with Rosamond close by, flushed and tearful, Will clasping both her upraised hands in his, speaking with low-toned fervor; in terrible illumination of certainty, paused motionless, laid down letter on small table, went quickly out
- **Immediate Response**: Directed coachman to Freshitt Hall; animated by self-possessed energy; determined to carry out purpose of telling Sir James and uncle about Lydgate; walked to schoolhouse and spoke with master and mistress about new bell
- **Night of Anguish**: Experienced waves of suffering shaking her thoroughly; cried in loud whispers between sobs after her lost belief in Will and lost joy of silent love; lay on bare floor as night grew cold; grand woman's frame shaken by sobs
- **Anguish's Two Objects**: Saw two images—Rosamond and Will—tearing her heart as if divided by sword; bright creature she had trusted; Will became changed belief exhausted of hope, detected illusion; fire of her anger flamed out in fitful returns of spurning reproach; questioned why he obtruded his life into hers, brought his cheap regard to her who had nothing paltry to give; knew he was deluding her
- **Morning Awakening**: Awoke in chill hours with clearest consciousness of looking into eyes of sorrow; wrapped warm things around her; seated herself in great chair; soul liberated from terrible conflict; no longer wrestling with grief but could sit with it as lasting companion; felt as if part of involuntary, palpitating life; asked "What should I do—how should I act now?"
- **Today's Second Visit to Lydgate's House**: Came to speak about injustice shown towards Lydgate; spoke quite simply, gathering firmness as she went on; told Rosamond her husband had warm friends who have not left off believing in his high character; explained Lydgate felt wrong not to pour out everything to Rosamond but could speak to Dorothea because she is indifferent person; emphasized that Lydgate feels his life bound into one with Rosamond's and his misfortunes hurt him more because they hurt her; spoke cordially with pleading tones
- **Discussion of Marriage**: With growing tremor, spoke of how marriage drinks up all power of giving or getting blessedness in other kinds of love; said even if one loved someone else better, it would be no use; spoke of how marriage murders other love and marriage stays like a murder; spoke of how if husband loved and trusted us and we have not helped him, we have made curse in his life
- **Emotional Breaking Point**: Voice sank very low; filled with need to express pitying fellowship rather than rebuke; put hands on Rosamond's; said with agitated rapidity that she knows the feeling may be very dear, taken hold of unawares, hard like death to part with, we are weak; waves of her own sorrow rushed over her with conquering force; stopped in speechless agitation, feeling inwardly grappled; face became of deathlier paleness, lips trembled; pressed hands helplessly
- **Reconciliation with Rosamond**: When Rosamond, taken hold of by emotion stronger than her own, hurried along in new movement, could find no words but involuntarily put her lips to Dorothea's forehead which was very near; for a minute the two women clasped each other as if they had been in a shipwreck
- **Revelation from Rosamond**: Rosamond disclosed that Will was telling her how he loved another woman so she might know he could never love Rosamond; said Will hates her because Dorothea mistook him yesterday; said Will claims it is through Rosamond that Dorothea will think ill of him, think he is false person; said he has never had any love for her and always thought slightly of her; said Will told her yesterday that no other woman existed for him beside Dorothea; said the blame of what happened is entirely hers; said Will could never explain to Dorothea because of her; said Dorothea could never think well of him again; but said she has now told Dorothea and he cannot reproach her anymore
- **Revulsion of Feeling**: Revulsion of feeling too strong to be called joy; tumult in which terrible strain of night and morning made resistant pain; could only perceive this would be joy when she recovered her power of feeling it; immediate consciousness one of immense sympathy without check; cared for Rosamond without struggle now; responded earnestly to her last words

**Will Ladislaw**
- Passionate love for Dorothea which he forbade himself to utter
- **Public Scandal**: Genealogy now public knowledge via Bambridge's disclosure; described as having "queer genealogy"—high-spirited young lady, musical Polish patriot, with "grafting of the Jew pawnbroker"
- **Scene at Lydgate's House**: Seated with Rosamond on sofa, clasping both her upraised hands, speaking with low-toned fervor; when Rosamond became aware of Dorothea's presence and snatched away her hands, Will looked round also; meeting Dorothea's eyes with new lightning in them, seemed changing to marble
- **Anguish After Dorothea's Departure**: Stood motionless with Rosamond; looked towards spot where Dorothea stood; said sharply "Don't touch me!" with utterance like cut of lash; darted from Rosamond; wheeled round to other side of room with tips of fingers in pockets and head thrown back, looking fiercely; had horrible inclination to shatter Rosamond with his anger
- **Emotional Eruption to Rosamond**: Expressed to Rosamond: "I had no hope before—not much—of anything better to come. But I had one certainty—that she believed in me. Whatever people had said or done about me, she believed in me.—That's gone! She'll never again think me anything but a paltry pretence"; spoke of inability to explain: "Explain! Tell a man to explain how he dropped into hell! I never had a _preference_ for her, any more than I have a preference for breathing. No other woman exists by the side of her."; told Rosamond that no other woman existed for him beside Dorothea; told her she must know he could never love her

**Rosamond Lydgate**
- Married to Lydgate; victorious obstinacy never wasting energy
- **Crisis Response**: When scandal broke, shock was terrible; felt shame was worst part of crime
- **Before Yesterday's Scene**: Regained brilliant health; determined to tell Will Ladislaw everything when he comes; morning descended equipped for walk with letter to Mr. Ladislaw written with charming discretion
- **Scene at Lydgate's House**: With bonnet hanging back, sat flushed and tearful, turned towards Will who leaned towards her clasping both her upraised hands; when Dorothea entered, snatched away her hands and rose
- **Will's Anger**: Had no sense of chill resolute repulsion such as known under Lydgate's displeasure; all her sensibility turned into bewildering novelty of pain; felt new terrified recoil under lash never experienced before; when Will ceased to speak, became image of sickened misery with pale lips and eyes with tearless dismay; after he left, tried to get up but fell back fainting; when came to herself, felt too ill to make exertion of rising; remained helpless until girl looked for her
- **Morning After**: Sat languidly wondering what to do next; looked ill but recovered her usual quietude; Lydgate feared to disturb her by any questions; Lydgate told her of Dorothea's letter with check and that Ladislaw sat with him last night; Rosamond made no reply
- **Response to Dorothea's Second Visit**: Colored and gave startled movement when Lydgate said Mrs. Casaubon come to see her again; did not say no despite daring not touch yesterday's facts; wondered why Dorothea came again; Will's lacerating words made every thought of Dorothea fresh smart; in humiliating uncertainty dared do nothing but comply; rose and let Lydgate put light shawl over her shoulders; requested Martha not bring anyone else into drawing-room; inwardly wrapped her soul in cold reserve; prepared to meet every word with polite impassibility; Will had bruised her pride too sorely to feel any compunction towards him and Dorothea
- **During Dorothea's Visit**: Under first great shock that shattered her dream-world; strange unexpected manifestation of Dorothea's feeling made her soul totter with sense she had been walking in unknown world just broken in upon her; convulsed throat subsiding into calm; when withdrew handkerchief hiding her face, eyes met Dorothea's helplessly as if they had been blue flowers; pride broken down between the two women
- **Rosamond's Disclosure to Dorothea**: Got more and more hurried as she spoke; said Will was telling her how he loved another woman so she might know he could never love her; said Will now hates her because Dorothea mistook him yesterday; said Will claims it is through her that Dorothea will think ill of him, think he is false person; said he has never had any love for her and always thought slightly of her; said he told her yesterday no other woman existed for him beside Dorothea; said blame of what happened is entirely hers; said he could never explain to Dorothea because of her; said now she has told Dorothea and he cannot reproach her anymore
- **Question About Lydgate**: Asked "Tertius did not find fault with me, then?" understanding now that Lydgate might have said anything to Mrs. Casaubon and that she certainly was different from other women; perhaps faint taste of jealousy in the question; a smile began to play over Dorothea's face

**Lydgate (Return from Coleman's)**
- Came home again after noticing Dorothea walking and sky changing, thinking rain might come; said he came back in quality of doctor, haunted by two pale faces—Mrs. Casaubon looked as much in need of care as Rosamond; thought he had not done his duty leaving them together; offered to send someone to order Dorothea's carriage

## Incidental Details - Rumors/Unverified Claims
- Only Cotho Hollwood knew that the Lindson family once owed a blood debt to the Hollmere family
- Only Breena Orlwood knew that the Lindson mill ledger was rewritten after the flood
- Only Cotho Hollwood knew that the fire at the Salford granary was set on purpose
- Only Breena Orlwood knew that the old abbey at Salford hides a second cellar

## Artifacts
- The jade ring belonged to Orvie Hollett
- Brevie Hollmere kept the amber mirror in a cedar box
- The jade chalice belonged to Islan Lindner, head of the Lindner household
